legacy_root.title: Choose a machine-checkable argumentation format for council argument graphs
legacy_root.question: Between IBIS, Toulmin-structured claims and formal argumentation frameworks, which can be mechanically checked for an unsupported claim or an unanswered rebuttal - and which is cheap enough for an agent to emit reliably?
legacy_root.answer: Choose IBIS-shaped typed graphs (Issue/Position/Argument with supports and objects-to, equivalently council SUPPORTS/ATTACKS/REBUTS) as the machine-checkable argumentation format. Write the unanswered-rebuttal check over objects-to edges whose attacker is undefended. Do not require agents to emit a Dung AF. Do not treat classic Toulmin Rebuttal as a reply graph.
legacy_root.recommendation: Choose IBIS-shaped typed graphs (Issue/Position/Argument with supports and objects-to, equivalently council SUPPORTS/ATTACKS/REBUTS) as the machine-checkable argumentation format. Write the unanswered-rebuttal check over objects-to edges whose attacker is undefended. Do not require agents to emit a Dung AF. Do not treat classic Toulmin Rebuttal as a reply graph.
legacy_root.schema_note: command-center/schema/research-claim-record.schema.json is absent (RES-0001 not delivered on this tree). This record is self-describing and carries claim id, canonical mechanism, source lineage/rails, evidence tier, confidence band, named settling probe, edges, freshness, and snapshot sha256 per rail.

format_comparison.name: IBIS / gIBIS (Issue, Position, Argument)
format_comparison.emit_cost_reason: Three node types and two edge types (supports, objects-to). Agents already emit issue/position/pro/con trees.

format_comparison.name: Toulmin six-element layout
format_comparison.emit_cost_reason: Six named slots; agents typically fill Claim+Data and skip Warrant/Backing. Rebuttal slot exists but is not a reply graph.
format_comparison.unanswered_rebuttal_check: UNCHECKABLE on classic six-element Toulmin: Rebuttal is an 'unless' circumstance attached to the warrant, not a node that can be answered. There is no named field for a reply-to-rebuttal. A check that looked at record.rebuttal being non-empty would only detect presence of a caveat, not whether it was answered. Marked uncheckable rather than faked.

format_comparison.name: Dung abstract argumentation framework
format_comparison.emit_cost_reason: TOO COSTLY for an agent to emit reliably: the agent must segment natural language into atomic arguments and a binary attack relation (argument mining). Computing grounded/admissible semantics is cheap once the graph exists; emitting the graph from council turns is the expensive, lossy step. Council IMP-0313 already asks for SUPPORTS/ATTACKS/REBUTS on turns — that is IBIS-shaped, not a Dung AF.
format_comparison.unsupported_claim_check: UNCHECKABLE natively: a Dung AF has only an attack relation. There is no support/grounds field, so 'unsupported claim' has no named field to read. Bipolar AFs add support; that is a different format.

control.requirement: at least one format marked uncheckable or too costly to emit

claims.claim: IBIS/gIBIS graphs with Issue, Position, Argument and supports/objects-to edges admit a mechanical unanswered-rebuttal check (objects-to edge whose attacker has no incoming objects-to) and a mechanical unsupported-position check (position with no supports edge).
claims.strongest_caveat: The check is structural, not semantic: a vacuous or off-topic objects-to node still 'answers' a rebuttal.

rails.quote: gIBIS implements Issue Based Information Systems (IBIS) and facilitates building and browsing typed IBIS networks (Conklin & Begeman, ACM TOIS 1988, DOI 10.1145/58566.59297).
The elements of IBIS are: issues, each associated with alternative positions, which are associated with arguments which support or object to a given position (pros/cons).

claims.claim: Classic six-element Toulmin layouts can be checked for missing Data/Grounds, but unanswered rebuttal is uncheckable: Rebuttal is an unless-circumstance on the warrant, not a reply node.
claims.strongest_caveat: An extended Toulmin-on-a-graph with a reply-to-rebuttal field would become checkable; that is no longer classic Toulmin.

rails.quote: Toulmin, The Uses of Argument, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press, 2003, DOI 10.1017/CBO9780511840005 (Crossref work record).
Rebuttal (Reservation): statements recognizing restrictions which may legitimately be applied to the claim. The second triad qualifier, backing, and rebuttal may not be needed.

claims.claim: A Dung AF (AR, attacks) admits a mechanical unanswered-rebuttal check (attack whose attacker is unattacked; cf. Def. 6 acceptability). Native unsupported-claim is uncheckable (no support field). Emitting a faithful AF from council NL is too costly for an agent: it is argument mining, not slot filling.
claims.strongest_caveat: Once an AF already exists, semantics are cheap. The cost is emission from natural-language turns, not the labelling algorithm.

rails.quote: Dung, On the acceptability of arguments and its fundamental role in nonmonotonic reasoning, logic programming and n-person games, Artificial Intelligence 77(2), 1995, DOI 10.1016/0004-3702(94)00041-X.
AF = (AR, attacks); an argument A is acceptable wrt S iff every attacker of A is attacked by S (author PDF of the 1995 paper).

claims.claim: For this repo's council argument graphs (IMP-0313 typed SUPPORTS/ATTACKS/REBUTS on turns), IBIS is the format that is both mechanically checkable for unsupported claims and unanswered rebuttals and cheap enough for an agent to emit. Toulmin fails the unanswered-rebuttal check; Dung AF fails emit-cost.
claims.strongest_caveat: IMP-0313 is a catalog target, not a shipped extractor on this tree (tools/council/artifacts/argument_graph.py is absent).

rails.quote: Semantic Scholar work record for Dung 1995 (DOI 10.1016/0004-3702(94)00041-X) — structured identifier rail independent of the Crossref JSON used in C-DUNG.
Dung defines acceptability: argument a is acceptable wrt E iff E defends a (every attacker is attacked by E). That is the labelling problem an agent would have to emit against.
